title: Robustness of Median-based Splitting Rules for Causal Trees
abstract: arXiv:2611.00348v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Causal forests (Athey and Imbens, 2016) are a widely used method for the estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Standard implementations use mean-based splitting criteria, which perform well when the outcome distribution is well-behaved and free of contamination, such as outliers or heavy tails. However, real-world data are rarely clean. Outcome perturbations can affect the tree structure selected by mean-based splitting rules and lead to unreliable treatment effect estimates. In this study, we systematically examine the robustness of causal forests to irregularities in the outcome distribution. translated_title: 因果树中基于中位数的分裂规则的稳健性研究
translated_abstract: 因果森林（Athey and Imbens, 2016）是一种被广泛用于估计异质性处理效应的方法。标准实现采用基于均值的分裂准则，当结果分布表现良好且未受污染（例如不存在离群值或厚尾）时，这些准则表现良好。然而，现实世界中的数据很少是干净的。结果的扰动会影响基于均值的分裂规则所选择的树结构，并导致不可靠的处理效应估计。在本研究中，我们系统地检验了因果森林对结果分布不规则性的鲁棒性。基于 Maßmann 和 Gliszczyńska-Schroeder（2026）提出的基于中位数的分裂准则，我们实证研究了三种基于中位数的分裂准则：中位数绝对偏差（MAD）、最小中位数平方（LMS）和中位数平方偏差（MSD）。我们进行了蒙特卡洛实验，并将这些方法应用于实际数据（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 本研究通过蒙特卡洛实验系统评估了三种基于中位数的分裂准则（MAD、LMS、MSD），证明当结果分布受离群值或厚尾污染时，这些准则比传统基于均值的因果森林分裂规则更为稳健。
en_tdlr: This study systematically evaluates three median-based splitting criteria (MAD, LMS, MSD) for causal forests via Monte Carlo experiments, demonstrating that they are more robust than standard mean-based splitting rules when outcome distributions are contaminated by outliers or heavy tails.
